annotationRationale: The Pythagorean theorem identifies the unshared sides, and the two triangle areas determine the needed fourth powers. The difference-of-squares identity evaluates the final product.
sourceMethod: Follows the official shared-length variables, area equations, and fourth-power calculation. Clarifies why the shared lengths are distinct and why the hypotenuse assignment is forced by the areas.

review.mathCheck: The shared lengths must be distinct, with the larger serving once as hypotenuse and once as leg. The areas give a²b²−a⁴=4 and a²b²=16, hence a⁴=12 and b⁴=64/3. The requested squared product is b⁴−a⁴=28/3, choice A. All possible shared-side roles are addressed.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 15 on page 6. It uses the same shared-side parametrization, area equations and fourth-power difference, while explaining why the side assignments are necessary.
review.annotationCheck: Pythagorean lengths and triangle areas are appropriately assessed; difference of squares is supporting algebra. The explanation is reconstructible at AMC 10 level.
